PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Centre

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Maternal Age: 38 years
Gestational Age: 12 weeks
Sample Type: Chorionic villus sample (CVS)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing for chromosomal abnormalities

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured chorionic villi using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific to chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. DNA was extracted from uncultured chorionic villi and amplified using multiplex PCR. Fragment analysis was performed on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. A minimum of four informative markers per chromosome were analyzed to assess for trisomy.

Markers analyzed:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S858, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S11, D21S1270, D21S1411

RESULTS
Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed

CONCLUSION
Normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormality detected by QF-PCR trisomy test.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect trisomies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. Other chromosomal abnormalities, including balanced rearrangements, mosaicism below 20%, and abnormalities of other chromosomes will not be detected by this method.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis from cultured chorionic villi to follow. This will provide comprehensive chromosomal analysis and exclude other chromosomal abnormalities not detected by QF-PCR.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
